# §5 Commerce Analytics — Highlights

## Summary
- **Subsections rendered:** 6 of 7
- **Subsections skipped:** 1 (Channel Breakdown → HAS_CART=false)
- **Period:** Trailing 12 months (Apr 2025–Mar 2026)

## Key Stats
1. **$1.44M in eCat GMV from 40 iPad orders at $36,040 AOV** — All eCat activity occurred in two bursts (3 orders in Apr 2025, 37 orders in Oct–Dec 2025), consistent with market-show-driven iPad ordering for this luxury fine furniture manufacturer. [→ §commerce]
2. **Zero eCat orders since December 2025** — No iPad orders have been submitted in the four months from January through April 2026, while all-channel business has continued at a steady 21–29 orders per month. The ordering gap is the most actionable signal in this section. [→ §commerce]
3. **Top 3 buyers account for 69.7% of eCat GMV** — Pavilion Broadway alone represents 36.1% ($457K) on 6 orders. Only 8 real buyers placed eCat orders in the trailing 12 months, reflecting a small, concentrated international dealer network. [→ §commerce]
4. **HFC orders dominate at 72.5% of volume and 94.8% of GMV** — Hold for Confirmation orders average $47,148, roughly 7× the $6,757 confirmed-order average, reflecting a deliberate approval workflow for large specification-grade transactions. [→ §commerce]
5. **35.1% GMV capture rate on 11.9% of order volume** — eCat orders average 3× the value of all-channel orders ($36,040 vs. $12,215 AOV). When reps use the iPad, they place the largest transactions in the business. [→ §commerce]

## Priority Action Candidate
- **HIGH**: eCat ordering has been dormant since December 2025 while all-channel business continues at full pace — reactivating iPad ordering for the next market cycle is the single highest-impact action for this account. The 35.1% GMV capture rate demonstrates the channel's value when active; the gap represents $1.4M+ in annualized high-value transactions that have reverted to other workflows. [→ §commerce]
